recipes.name: Sesame Noodle Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon sesame seeds, or more if desired

steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Once the water is boiling, stir in the angel hair pasta, and return to a boil. Cook the pasta uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the pasta has cooked through, but is still firm to the bite, 4 to 5 minutes. Drain well in a colander set in the sink.

Whisk together the sesame oil, soy sauce, balsamic vinegar, chili oil, and sugar in a large bowl. Toss the pasta in the dressing, then sprinkle with sesame seeds, green onion, and bell pepper. Serve warm, or cover and refrigerate for a cold salad.

raw_recipe.headline: Sesame Noodle Salad
raw_recipe.description: Served chilled or warm, this noodle salad easily pairs with your favorite summertime foods.

video.description: Watch this video to learn how to make an Asian-inspired noodle salad with angel hair pasta. It's super easy and will take you less than half an hour to prepare. While the pasta is boiling, whisk together sesame oil, soy sauce, hot chili oil and a few other ingredients and the dressing is ready. Load the salad up with your favorite vegetables for a vegetarian entree or add cooked chicken or shrimp.

review.reviewBody: Delicious! I cut the recipe in half as well as the amount of sesame oil and used low sodium soy sauce. I toasted my sesame seeds as well and added them at the end - they give a nice presentation. I would have never thought of adding balsamic vinegar! It was a really nice addition. And, this is great warm or cold - but I prefer it cold as it really does get better the next day!

Love the flavors in the salad! I scaled this recipe back a bit since I am only serving two people. I left out the hot chili oil because family members don't tolerate spiciness well. I used the angel hair pasta, boiled for 4 minutes then drained it and set it aside. I added 3T sesame oil, 4T soysauce, 2T balsamic vinegar but keeping almost the 1/4 cup of the white sugar called for in the recipe. I tased the sauce until it was the right balance with sweetness. I added the warm noodles into the sauce along with the chopped green onions and red bell peppers. I added more chopped green onions and a little yellow and orange bell peppers for color, texture and nutrition. At first the sauce will seem like a lot, however the warm noodles will soak it all up. I highly suggest chilling the noodles to allow the flavors to meld and come alive. Right before serving I sprinkled sesame seeds over the noodles for added presentation (see my picture in the photo gallery). A very colorful dish with peppers, green onions and sesame seeds. This salad is simply easy to prepare and flavorful. The balsamic vinegar is an interesting twist but it was not strong with all other ingredients. I always like the combination of the sesame oil with soy sauce and sugar. The sauce can easily be adjusted to fit your tastes. I served these noodles along with, "Hoisin-Ginger Beef Skewers," from this website and another tasty dish! The sesame noodle is best served chilled especially on a hot, humid day!
Excellent! I also added one half a green bell pepper and about one cup carrot matchsticks.

Very easy and infinitely adjustable. I load up with additional vegetables (the frozen edamame suggested by one commentator is a great idea), and add another protein such as chicken or shrimp, along with a little extra chili oil and sesame seeds. I make the full amount for just the two of us and we can eat it for multiple days.

I used vermicelli pasta and the veggies I had on hand. Julienne carrots,green beans,yellow squash,. I also added garlic chopped to my dressing. I used rice vinegar,sesame oil, tamari soy sauce. and red chili pepper. I let it marinate all day in the fridge before dinner. I couldn't wait to eat it. Yum.Also added toasted cashews and sesame seeds too top . So good.
MADE it HEALTHIER: Subbed Spiralled zucchini & carrots for the noodles. Blanced them for 1 minute to soften. Only used 2 tablespoons of white sugar instead of 1/4 cup! Thank you!!! Love it!

The only complaint I have is that it would be just as flavorful ,but healthier if it had more vegetables. I subbed apple cider vinegar for the rice wine vinegar (didn’t have any rice vine vinegar) and added more vegetables. I added some celery, a little diced onion, thawed frozen peas along with the carrots and red bell pepper. I used angel hair pasta, broken into 3-5” lengths. I find long pasta very hard to eat neatly. This is a recipe I plan on using in the future.
This has been my go to salad for luncheons. I use peanuts instead of sesame seeds and I also add 2-3 cooked chicken breasts cut into small chunks.

This is good - but way too sweet. I only added 2 tablespoons of sugar and that was enough for us. Also added chopped broccoli, carrots and pea pods. I used rice wine vinegar as well. We like this cold with grilled chicken teriyaki.

I make this with whole wheat spaghetti, which my family is generally not fond of, but it works great with this recipe. I've made it a few times, and served it both warm and chilled. I've also added thin strips of firm tofu for a bit of protein.

Awesome! Couldn't get enough! Next time I will use 24 oz of pasta (1.5 packages). *Do NOT sub* any other oil for the sesame oil. It is critical! I increased the amount of green onions and added matchstick carrots per another review.
This is an awesome noodle salad! I prefer to enjoy it as a cold salad. I always omit the chili oil, as I cannot tolerate anything spicy. I recommend giving this recipe a try!
So easy to make and so addictively delicious! I sometimes make a batch for school lunches- it keeps so well in the fridge! Also a big hit at parties. Everyone asks for the recipe!

I really liked it! Especially because I could control the ingredients. My wife has to watch her sodium intake so I used lower sodium soy sauce. The she could add as much as she wanted which I'm sure was a lot less that you'd find in prepackaged sesame noodles at the grocery store deli. I also used whole wheat fettuccine to make it kind of like low mein but also because whole wheat pasta is better for those who need to watch their blood sugar. Honesty, with the flavorful dressing, you'd never notice the difference. Makes a great side dish with teriyaki chicken wings!
Add peanut butter to dressing
So good. I’ve made this recipe a few times and it’s one of my favorites. I add a splash of Chardonnay to the sauce for a little extra sweetness. Chef’s kiss! Thank you!

This is a delicious recipe! I made it a day ahead and let the flavors marinate. It is delicious as is or with chicken or shrimp added in. I always get requests for the recipe after friends and family eat this dish.
Love this. I use butter nut squash seed oil and no peppers. It’s delicious.
I made this exactly according to recipie. Really really spicy hot. Must be the hot sesame oil. Next time I will use spaghetti and half of the hot oil
I loved it and so did my neighbors. I am going to make it again but with minced yellow or red onion.
